name: fixbench: which kind of fix delays the policy least, at equal safety (offline, counterfactual)
registered: 2026-10-24 ~19:00 EDT, before any bench branch was run
question: fixcf showed a G-CEM fix delays the grasp 1.36 chunks vs 0.41 chunk of motion removed (amplification): the policy detours after a deviation. Is the detour caused by the fix leaving the policy's own distribution? Then SELECTION among the policy's own samples (in-distribution, same certificate) should delay less. G-steer is measured on the same yardstick.
cases: the 150 fixcf decisions (eval/fix_counterfactual.py cases; seed 20261025): approach decisions where the 3x filter intervened, paired_cbfg3m_stl, no neighbour topple in the logged episode
harness: exactly fixcf: exact saved state d, 2-frame history rebuilt by replaying chunk d-1, the run's execution noise (scale 2), one first chunk per branch, then the policy alone for up to 30 chunks with the same denoising seed in every branch

branches.job ARMS=sel: nominal (policy's own chunk), gcem (the logged deployed fix), sel (16 fresh policy samples from the same history, seed 20261025+7+1000e+d; certified with the 3x filter's certificate: OIL+ENS, 64 fresh futures per model, h >= min(h_hold, 2), o <= O_MAX; the certified sample with the lowest opt2 change cost vs the policy's plan; none -> hold if certified, else best (h, -o), as opt2.finish), resample (control: sample 0, uncertified)
branches.job ARMS=steer: nominal, steer (G-steer recomputed at d with cbfgst3m's search and certificate, regardless of the trigger)

measures: as fixcf: grasp (gripper < 55), extract, neighbour topple (>= 45 deg); not grasped within 30 = 31
primary: delay(arm) = grasp(arm) - grasp(nominal, same job) on cases where neither branch toppled. PRIMARY: mean of delay(sel) - delay(gcem), paired over cases where neither of the four branches' relevant pairs toppled (sel/nominal and gcem/nominal); bootstrap (10000, seed 20261027) one-sided 95% upper bound < 0 AND topple non-inferiority: one-sided 95% upper bound of (topple(sel) - topple(gcem)) over all cases <= +3 pp -> PASS ('in-distribution fixes cost less time'). Otherwise FAIL.
secondary: mean delay of gcem, sel, resample (each with a 90% bootstrap interval); resample answers: does ANY different policy sample cost time? (if resample ~ gcem, the detour is about deviating at all, not about leaving the distribution)
sel kinds (certified / fallback hold / fallback best) and number certified of 16
steer: mean delay and steer - gcem (paired across jobs, each relative to its own nominal); topples
reproduction: nominal and gcem branches identical to fixcf rows (same harness, same cluster)
run: Fir, cluster/fixbench.sbatch: ARMS=sel 15 tasks x 10 cases, ARMS=steer 10 tasks x 15 cases; smoke 1 case each first (not analysed separately; it is case 0 of shard 0 and is kept)
next_if_pass: policy-guided sampling (barrier-gradient guidance inside the diffusion denoising) as the next fix arm on this bench, then a closed-loop test

amendment_1.written: 2026-10-24 ~19:20 EDT, before any bench branch ran (smokes still queued)
amendment_1.arm: job ARMS=proj: nominal, gcem, proj = the deployed fix projected onto the policy's distribution (SDEdit): the fix's 16-step plan (opt2 convention) noised to strength 0.25 of the policy's 8-step DDIM schedule and denoised by the policy with the same 2-frame observations, 8 samples (seed 20261025+9+1000e+d), certified as sel; the certified one with the lowest change cost vs the policy's plan; none certified -> the deployed fix
amendment_1.strength_choice: 0.25, from distances on 4 cases (no outcomes run): at 0.5 the projection drifted back toward the policy's own plan (proj-fix 5.6-7.2 mm vs fix size 3-8 mm); 0.25 stays nearer the fix (4.4-5.6 mm)
amendment_1.test: same primary form as sel: mean delay(proj) - delay(gcem), paired, one-sided 95% upper bound < 0 AND topple upper95 <= +3 pp -> PASS
amendment_1.observation: fresh policy samples differ from the policy's own plan by 3.9-11.5 mm (median of 8), as much as or more than the fixes (3-8 mm): the fix is not large relative to the policy's own sampling spread

amendment_2.written: 2026-10-24 ~19:50 EDT, after the 1-case smokes (outcomes of case 0 only seen)
amendment_2.finding: case 0 (ep 21003, d 15): the gcem branch extracted at chunk 11 on node fc11015 (sel job; = the fixcf row) but not within 30 chunks on fc11017 (proj job): continuations are node-dependent (as the cross-cluster checks before). Within a job all branches share one GPU.
amendment_2.change: the steer job also runs the gcem branch; steer vs gcem is paired within the job (no cross-job comparison). The steer smoke row (no gcem branch) is deleted and re-run. Every comparison in the analysis is within one job; reproduces_fixcf is reported as a node-consistency check, not a gate.

amendment_3.written: 2026-10-24 ~20:25 EDT, before any guide branch ran
amendment_3.arm: job ARMS=guide: nominal, gcem, guide = guided denoising: 4 policy samples from fresh noise (seed 20261025+11+1000e+d) with the same observations; in the last 4 of the 8 DDIM steps the x0 estimate moves by a normalised gradient step of size 0.05 (normalised action units) down the log total variance of the plan's imagined HOLD30 latents (model_OIL, 16 futures at 4x the errors, fixed perceived starts and execution noise per case, seed 20261025+13+1000e+d); certified as sel (OIL+ENS, 64 fresh futures); the certified one with the lowest change cost; none -> the deployed fix
amendment_3.step_choice: 0.05 from the surrogate only (4 cases, no outcome run): log tvar drop vs the unguided twin 0.13-0.65 with a median plan shift of 0.8-2.4 mm; 0.02 too weak (0.04-0.43); 0.10 overshoots (spread rose in 2 of 4)
amendment_3.test: same primary form: mean delay(guide) - delay(gcem), paired within the job, one-sided 95% upper bound < 0 AND topple upper95 <= +3 pp -> PASS; secondary: median log tvar drop

amendment_4.written: 2026-10-24 ~20:40 EDT, before any 1x branch ran and before any 2x bench result was seen (2x jobs still running)
amendment_4.question: (user) does running at 2x execution noise swamp the fine-grained fixes (steer, guided, projection, selection), so that only crude ones can help?
amendment_4.design: the same bench (all four jobs: sel, steer, proj, guide; same cases, seeds, certificates, arms) with the BRANCHES executed at 1x the measured execution noise (the same per-episode noise pattern at half the amplitude, eval/plausibility.episode_noises scale 1); the 2-frame history is still rebuilt with the run's own 2x noise so it stays exact. Output deep_dive/fixbench_n1, result results/jenga/fixbench_n1_result.json.
amendment_4.tests: per arm the same primary form as at 2x (delay(arm) - delay(gcem) one-sided 95% upper bound < 0 AND topple upper95 <= +3 pp). Interpretation fixed now: 'noise masks fine fixes' is supported if at least one of steer / guide / proj / sel passes at 1x while failing at 2x; if the arm-minus-gcem delays are about the same at 1x and 2x, noise is not what limits them. Also reported: nominal-branch topples and gcem's delay at 1x vs 2x (how much the filter's time cost depends on the noise).
